rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent folded-roof mass with one dominant diagonal gesture and a secondary support strip, so the overall hierarchy is legible. In all four views the volume stays consistent and does not visibly collide with itself, which supports repair integrity. However, the form still depends on stepback-like terracing along the section/profile, so the silhouette is only moderately non-stair. There is little evident public void, undercut, or courtyard logic; it is mostly a closed solid with a central seam rather than a spatially active carve. The precedent resonance is decent because the folded section recalls OMA/TAO-like roof-and-section operations, but it remains more generic and less spatially rich than the references.
warnings: Void logic is weak; the mass is primarily solid with only a narrow seam.
Sectional folding reads more as stepped massing than as a clearly carved public void.
Could become more legible if one primary anchor volume is strengthened and small terrace pieces reduced.
